preamble: De-retroflexion of the voiceless retroflex affricate [ʈʂ] to alveolar [ts] merges the retroflex and dental sibilant series. In colloquial Taiwanese Mandarin, Standard Mandarin zh- is pronounced as z- in most contexts. Most Southwestern Mandarin varieties, including Chengdu Sichuanese, merge zh, ch and sh with z, c and s, so Standard zhōng and zhēn correspond to Sichuanese zong1 and zen1. Polish mazuration (cz > c) is not included here: it acted on the older palato-alveolar [tʃ], before Polish developed retroflexes.

examples.note: Colloquial Taiwan Guoyu pronounces zh-, ch- and sh- like z-, c- and s- in most contexts.
The same merger applies to every zh- syllable.
Most Southwestern Mandarin varieties merge the retroflex series with the alveolar affricates and fricatives.

examples.from: Standard Mandarin 中 zhōng, 真 zhēn
examples.note: The correspondence is regular in Sichuanese Pinyin across zh- syllables.
